body:
# Phase directive — «Standing live rig with a screen model» (Epoch 4's first entry, viola-0.2.0, v2-32)

1. Scope is the route entry and its SIX carries as they stand at `bd95971c`: one reusable live rig — a terminal
   screen model, kept screens, the CLI's trust and modal dialogs read — that later live rounds reuse. Re-measure at
   P3, from the code and the evidence the earlier live rounds landed (`live-*.py`, `survey-rig.py`, their reports):
   what each rig built for itself, what each got wrong, and what a standing rig must own so none is rebuilt.
2. **The rig owns its isolation (the founder's ruling, 2026-11-17, the sixth carry):** a scratch root outside every
   repository, a private config dir, a credentials copy guarded by the token-window read (refuse a start under 20
   minutes of token left, uncounted) and removed on every exit path, no write to his real `~/.claude.json` left
   unexplained, no host path and nothing of his status line or config in a record. Built and CHECKED once: the
   plan names the check that proves each of these on the fake agent, with no live start.
3. **A measured fault of the last rig, for the plan to close:** a killed test or mutant run left booted wrappers
   alive for hours (ten processes of the 2026-11-17 audit, re-parented, their executables deleted). The rig — and
   any booted test it stands for — ends what it starts on every exit path, its own kill deadline included; say how
   the plan proves that (a census of processes under the rig's own scratch root at exit, or a stronger means).
4. **SIZE FIRST — this entry carries more than one window may hold.** Beside the rig itself the carries pin live
   READINGS onto it: what the CLI trims at submit (leading, trailing, inside a paste); the hook-latency window of
   v2-19; whether a fired scheduled wake's prompt carries `source`, and «a real wake reads 1»; the record-home
   rule's live half; the fake agent's DEL and modal fidelity. At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block:
   (a) the steps and files the rig alone needs, and whether rig + every carried reading fits one implement window
   (the last take-ups ended their phase at 50–62 % of a window; say your own at that point);
   (b) if it does not fit, a split named plainly — what stays in this chunk (the lean: the rig, its isolation and
   process hygiene, its rehearsal, and the fewest readings that PROVE the rig on the real CLI) and what goes to a
   following entry «first readings on the standing rig» — the placement is the founder's, do not take it;
   (c) the live starts: for each reading the SHAPE first (what makes the screen or the event appear, what closes it,
   who holds the wheel at the key, what the start reads if the thing does not show — three of six starts were
   lost to shape in the survey chunk), then the exact count, the keys the rig types into its own pty, and what the
   chunk loses without them. The cap and the keys are the founder's, per chunk; the overseer brings them to him
   with (b) in one dialog. Plan every other step on the fake agent meanwhile.
5. No mutation run. Name each control's `--timeout S` in the plan's prose, on an entry filtered to the guard's own
   cases; a control id stays within 16 characters; «holds» = those cases ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Every
   acceptance predicate is one that CAN fail: say for each what change would turn it red.
6. A test that waits on a channel or a thread takes a bound; none can hang past a failure. A test socket goes under
   the short `/tmp` root; a stamped home comes from the shared stamp's copy.
7. A fold is decided at the PHASE. If implement meets a red that moves a plan entry it stops and says so BEFORE the
   operator pass. Every acceptance threshold is checked at P4 against the class's own `ci` and `mutants` kills.
8. A fork that is the founder's (a boundary widening, a live cap, a typed key, a placement) is asked through the
   overseer, who brings it to him by dialog — he is present, slow to answer; a technical fork is answered by relay
   at once.
9. Set NO scheduled wake or timer of your own. If a hook refuses such a call, quote its line on the card.
10. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; rows read whole or by search; whether EVERY cited row is in
    the union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` /
    `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-17-standing-live-rig · **Version:** viola-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-17T06:40:44Z

Stand ONE committed live rig, the test-only binary `viola-live-rig` in `viola-e2e`, that every later live round
reuses instead of writing its own `live-*.py` scripts. It hosts a child (`claude`, `viola run … -- claude`, or the
fake agent) on a pty it owns, keeps a vt100 screen model of what the child draws, reads the trust dialog and the input
box by compiled literals (the box through the product's one readiness predicate,
`viola_agent_claude::screen::SIGNATURES.input_box_up`), keeps its screens only under a gitignored local path with one
closed-word summary per frame (security-plan · decision/live-session-screens-kept-local), and types only the keys the
founder granted (security-plan · decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty; inputs#I2 item 2).

The rig owns its isolation and its processes (inputs#I1 items 2–3; inputs#I2 item 3): a scratch root outside every
repository, a private config dir, a credentials copy guarded by the token-window read and removed on every exit path,
`~/.claude.json` read before and after each start with any change named, no host path, credential, status line or
config value in any record; its child in its own process group, a watchdog deadline, and a `/proc` census at every exit
that must read zero before the scratch root is removed. The fake agent gains the two fidelities the rig reads live:
DEL erases, and the trust dialog has a selector the trust key passes. Two live starts (R1 trust + DEL, R2 whitespace
trim at submit), plus one spare re-fire, prove the rig on the real CLI under the founder's cap (inputs#I2 item 2). The
committed rig widens test-plan · decision/live-readings-not-a-test-layer on the founder's own word (inputs#I2 item 4).

Split out by the founder (inputs#I2 items 1, 3), not this chunk's: R3 (the fired wake's `source`, «a real wake reads
1», the hook-latency window) and R4 (the live `viola verify --record`) go to the new entry «first readings on the
standing rig»; a booted wrapper outliving its SIGKILLed test is its own new entry, second in Epoch 4.

1. **Crate wiring.** `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml`: a `[[bin]]` `viola-live-rig` at `src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` with a
   one-line comment like its siblings, and `vt100.workspace = true` (the workspace pin `=0.16.2`, already in the graph
   through `viola-agent-claude`: no new crate). `crates/viola-e2e/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod rig;`. Keeps tests S-list lines
   on test-only bins and exact pins (tests-standing; arch-standing).

2. **Screen model** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs`: a vt100 `Parser` at 45×210 fed every drained byte under
   `catch_unwind` (a caught panic poisons the model; its frames read `poisoned`), rows read top to bottom. Readings, each
   a closed word, never row text: `box` (`up` when `SIGNATURES.input_box_up(&rows)`), `trust` (`shown` when a row holds
   `Yes, I trust this folder`), `selected` (`trust-yes` when the row holding that literal also holds the selector glyph
   `❯`, `other-row` when another row holds it, `none`), `options` (the count of rows holding a numbered or `❯`-led option
   inside the dialog, `0` when none), `box-text` (`empty` when the box's prompt row is `❯` and spaces alone, `holds-text`
   otherwise — no character of it kept), `modal` (`imports` for `Yes, allow external imports`, `none`). The literal set is
   compiled in the module, the trust and imports literals copied from `SIGNATURES.modals` by reference, never typed again.

3. **Isolation** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`:
   a. scratch root `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/<run>` made 0700 through `viola_state::fs::create_private_dir` (a `/tmp` base,
      outside every repository; `--scratch-base` overrides it for the rehearsal tests only), holding the start's `cwd/`,
      its private config dir `config/` (the child gets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<root>/config`) and, for a wrapped start, a
      viola home `vhome/` (no component named `home`: the record-home rule's rig half, test-plan ·
      decision/record-home-names-no-home);
   b. the credentials copy: `--credentials` (default `~/.claude/.credentials.json`) read through `take(MAX_FRAME)`, its
      `claudeAiOauth.expiresAt` alone parsed; absent, not a number or under 20 minutes from now refuses the start
      `token-window` before the ledger line (uncounted); else the bytes are placed into `config/.credentials.json` by
      `viola_state::fs::place_private_new` (0600 mode-first) and never read again;
   c. a seeded `config/.claude.json` (the onboarding-complete keys the survey rig seeded; for R2 the start's `cwd` marked
      trusted) written 0600;
   d. `~/.claude.json` (`--user-config` overrides it for the rehearsals) read before the spawn and after the census:
      sha256 prefix and mtime compared, the reading `user-config: unchanged | changed | absent`, the bytes never kept;
   e. the child's environment built from scratch: `HOME USER LOGNAME SHELL PATH LANG XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` kept, `TERM`
      set `xterm-256color`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and the run marker `AGENT_RUN_RIG=<run>` added, every other name absent
      (arch · decision/harness-env-var-prefix); `PATH` gets the stamped CLI's install dir first and `claude --version`
      is read by path before the ledger line (verification-harness.md 2026-10-10);
   f. teardown on every exit path (a guard whose `Drop` runs it): census (step 4) → remove the credentials copy → remove
      the scratch root → read it absent. A refusal before the root exists removes nothing.

4. **Processes** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/procs.rs`: the child spawned through `viola_pty::spawn` (its own session
   and process group); a watchdog thread with the start's deadline (`--deadline`, default 600 s for R1/R2, the rehearsal's
   own short one): at the deadline, or on the rig's SIGINT/SIGTERM, Ctrl-C into the pty every 500 ms, SIGKILL of the
   group at 10 s. The census: every `/proc/<pid>` whose `environ` holds `AGENT_RUN_RIG=<run>` or whose `cwd` lies under
   the scratch root; non-empty → SIGKILL each by pid + start time (`viola_state::liveness::start_times`), census again, and
   the start's summary reads `census: <n> killed` (0 is the passing reading). `viola-live-rig census [--kill]` runs the
   same census over every `AGENT_RUN_RIG` marker (a start whose rig was SIGKILLed is swept at the next start, which
   refuses `leftover` until `census --kill` runs). Sends at no process it did not start
   (testing.md 2026-10-10).

5. **Keys** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs`: the grant parsed from `--grant trust,box` (absent = none); trust
   keys (≤2 `ESC [ B`, then one `\r`) only while `trust: shown` reads, the Enter only on `selected: trust-yes`; box keys
   (one `x`, one `0x7f`) only while `box: up`; `\x03` only by the stop. Every key typed is counted into the summary by
   name, never by byte; a key outside the grant is a refusal `key-not-granted`, nothing written.

6. **Ledger, kept screens, summary** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/ledger.rs`: `--ledger <file>` ndjson, one line before a
   start (`{label, ts}`, `ts` from `date -u`), one closed-word summary after; `--cap N` refuses `spent` (label already
   ledgered) and `cap` (N starts ledgered) before the line, uncounted; the CLI version by path other than `--cli`
   refuses `version`, uncounted. Frames kept under `target/live-rig/<run>/screens/` (gitignored by the root `target/`
   rule), one per settle and per key, each with its closed-word summary line in `target/live-rig/<run>/frames.ndjson`;
   the summary names the settle's wait in ms (testing.md 2026-10-06).

7. **Entry** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`: `rehearse <arm>` (the fake agent as the child, given by
   `--program`), `live <label>` (`R1`, `R2`, or the spare `R1-2` / `R2-2`), `census [--kill]`. `live` refuses `ci` when
   `CI` is set (test-plan · decision/live-readings-not-a-test-layer as widened, inputs#I2 item 4). R1: a bare `claude` in
   `cwd/` (no git repo, no `CLAUDE.md`): settle, read the trust frame, the trust keys, settle, read the box, `x`, settle,
   DEL, settle, read `box-text`, stop. R2: `viola run --home <root>/vhome --name rig-r2 -- claude` in a seeded-trusted
   `cwd/`; after `box: up`, three `viola send rig-r2 --file` texts (leading spaces; trailing spaces then a TAB; an inner
   run of spaces and an inner LF), each read from `events.ndjson`'s `prompt-submitted` through the complete-lines reader
   and summarised `equal | leading-trimmed | trailing-trimmed | inner-changed` against the typed text; a refused send
   reads `not-delivered:<detail>`, no retry; no key typed (the wheel stays the driver's). A trust dialog seen on R2 types
   nothing and reads `trust: shown` (a start lost to shape: the spare). Each `viola` the rig starts drops `VIOLA_NAME`,
   `VIOLA_DIR` and `VIOLA_BIN` (test-plan · decision/test-started-viola-drops-env).

8. **Fake-agent DEL** — `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs`: a `0x7f` outside a paste removes the prompt's last
   character (UTF-8 aware) and is receipted as its `key`; on an empty prompt it removes nothing.

9. **Fake-agent trust selector** — `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`: under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd, the modal is
   drawn with a selector row (`❯` before the trust literal, a second numbered option under it); a down-arrow moves the
   selector, Enter on the trust row draws `Screen.ready` and fires the launch SessionStart, Enter on the other row exits
   1; no hook fires before it. The rows drawn are compiled literals in the fake agent, copied from R1's closed-word
   summary (step 12 aligns them if R1 reads otherwise). `contract_fake_agent_drift` stays green: no recorded set moves.

10. **Rehearsal tests** — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` (labelled case table rows in `#[test]`s, viola-e2e
    takes no rstest; every wait under `WITHIN`, the child owned and killed at a stated deadline; keeps tests S-list lines
    on bounded waits and owned children): one case per predicate of `## Acceptance Criteria` A1–A9, each driving the
    built `viola-live-rig rehearse` over the fake agent with a planted canary credentials file
    (`AGENT_RUN_CANARY_7f3e` token), `--scratch-base` under the short `/tmp` test root and `--user-config` a planted
    file.

11. **Rig unit cases** — inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `rig/screen.rs` (each reading over fed byte strings,
    the poison), `rig/isolate.rs` (the token-window boundary at 20 min ± 1 s, the env built), `rig/keys.rs` (the grant).

12. **Live R1** (leg, fired by `gate.py run --live-legs` in the order below, after steps 1–11 are green): the R1 summary
    is read; where its `options`/`selected` words differ from the fake's rehearsal summary for the same arm, step 9's
    compiled rows are corrected to them and step 10 re-run before R2. A start lost to shape takes the spare (`R1-2`)
    once, on the operator's word; none left → the reading stays `unread` and A10 reads red.
13. **Live R2** (leg, after R1's step 12 closes).

14. **Records** — `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-17-standing-live-rig/evidence/live-starts.md`: each start's ledger
    line and summary, verbatim, and the cap's state (`starts 2 of 2 + spare unspent | spent on <label>`).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — the rig's entry (`rehearse` · `live` · `census`).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/` — `mod.rs`, `screen.rs`, `isolate.rs`, `procs.rs`, `keys.rs`, `ledger.rs`.
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the fake-agent rehearsal cases A1–A9.
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — the `[[bin]]` and the `vt100` workspace dependency.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod rig;`.
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs` — DEL erases.
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the trust selector and its keys.

The rig's rehearsals are ordinary tests on the fake agent and run in CI; its live arm refuses under `CI`. The two
live legs run by hand under the founder's cap (inputs#I2 item 2) through `gate.py run --live-legs`; the `round` probe
before them reads the stamped CLI by path, primes nothing. No boot-path touchpoint (the product binary is unchanged):
no `smoke` entry. No mutation run (inputs#I1 item 5). The acceptance needs CI (the rehearsals as CI tests), so the
operator pass carries hygiene, pre-push, push and the CI read.

Remove-the-guard controls, each implement's one-shot `gate.py control` (never an entry), each fired on entry 4's
form filtered to the guard's own case, `--timeout 60`, «holds» = the named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line:

- `rig-census` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/procs.rs`: the census's kill-and-recount removed (teardown reads 0 without
  looking); case `rig_ends_what_it_starts_on_every_exit_path`.

- `rig-cred-rm` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`: the credentials copy's removal in teardown removed; case
  `rig_leaves_no_credentials_copy_on_any_exit_path`.

- `rig-token` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`: the 20-minute comparison removed; case
  `rig_refuses_a_start_under_twenty_minutes_of_token`.

- `rig-keygrant` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs`: the grant check removed; case
  `rig_types_no_key_outside_its_grant`.

- `fake-del` — `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/input.rs`: the `0x7f` arm removed; case
  `rig_rehearsal_reads_the_box_empty_after_x_and_del` (entry 4).
A `timeout` reading on any of them reads the control NOT held.
